1.1: And Moab transgresses against Israel after the death of Ahab,
1.2: and Ahaziah falls through the lattice in his upper chamber that is in Samaria, and is sick, and sends messengers, and says to them, `Go you, inquire of Baal-Zebub god of Ekron if I recover from this sickness.'
1.3: And a messenger of Jehovah has spoken to Elijah the Tishbite, `Rise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and speak to them, Is it because there is not a God in Israel--you are going to inquire of Baal Zebub god of Ekron?
1.4: and therefore, thus said Jehovah, The bed where you have gone up, you do not come down from it, for you do certainly die;' and Elijah goes on.
1.5: And the messengers turn back to him, and he says to them, `What is this--you have turned back!'
1.6: And they say to him, `A man has come up to meet us, and says to us, Go, turn back to the king who sent you, and you have said to him, Thus said Jehovah, Is it because there is not a God in Israel--you are sending to inquire of Baal-Zebub god of Ekron? therefore, the bed where you have gone up, you do not come down from it, for you do certainly die.'
1.7: And he says to them, `What is the fashion of the man who has come up to meet you, and speaks to you these words?'
1.8: And they say to him, `A man--hairy, and a girdle of skin girt about his loins;' and he says, `He is Elijah the Tishbite.'
1.9: And he sends to him a head of fifty and his fifty, and he goes up to him (and indeed, he is sitting on the top of the hill), and he speaks to him, `O man of God, the king has spoken, Come down.'
1.10: And Elijah answers and speaks to the head of the fifty, `And if I am a man of God, fire does come down from the heavens, and consume you and your fifty;' and fire comes down from the heavens, and consumes him and his fifty.
1.11: And he turns and sends to him another head of fifty and his fifty, and he answers and speaks to him, `O man of God, thus said the king, Haste, come down.'
1.12: And Elijah answers and speaks to them, `If I am a man of God, fire does come down from the heavens, and consume you and your fifty;' and fire of God comes down from the heavens, and consumes him and his fifty.
1.13: And he turns and sends a third head of fifty and his fifty, and the third head of fifty goes up, and comes in, and bows on his knees over-against Elijah, and makes supplication to him, and speaks to him, `O man of God, let be precious, I pray you, my soul and the soul of your servants--these fifty--in your eyes.
1.14: Indeed, come down has fire from the heavens, and consumes the two heads of the former fifties and their fifties; and, now, let my soul be precious in your eyes.'
1.15: And a messenger of Jehovah speaks to Elijah, `Go down with him, be not afraid of him;' and he rises and goes down with him to the king,
1.16: and speaks to him, `Thus said Jehovah, Because that you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-Zebub god of Ekron--is it because there is not a God in Israel to inquire of His word? therefore, the bed where you have gone up--you do not come down from it, for you do certainly die.'
1.17: And he dies, according to the word of Jehovah that Elijah spoke, and Jehoram reigns in his stead, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, for he had no son.
1.18: And the rest of the matters of Ahaziah that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?

2.1: And it comes to pass, at Jehovah's taking up Elijah in a whirlwind to the heavens, that Elijah goes, and Elisha, from Gilgal,
2.2: and Elijah says to Elisha, `Abide, I pray you, here, for Jehovah has sent me to Beth-El;' and Elisha says, `Jehovah lives, and your soul lives, if I leave you;' and they go down to Beth-El.
2.3: And sons of the prophets who are in Beth-El come out to Elisha, and say to him, `Have you known that to-day Jehovah is taking your lord from your head?' and he says, `I also have known--keep silent.'
2.4: And Elijah says to him, `Elisha, abide, I pray you, here, for Jehovah has sent me to Jericho;' and he says, `Jehovah lives, and your soul lives, if I leave you;' and they come in to Jericho.
2.5: And sons of the prophets who are in Jericho come nigh to Elisha, and say to him, `Have you known that to-day Jehovah is taking your lord from your head?' and he says, `I also have known--keep silent.'
2.6: And Elijah says to him, `Abide, I pray you, here, for Jehovah has sent me to the Jordan;' and he says, `Jehovah lives, and your soul lives, if I leave you;' and they go on both of them,
2.7: --and fifty men of the sons of the prophets have gone on, and stand over-against afar off--and both of them have stood by the Jordan.
2.8: And Elijah takes his robe, and wraps it together, and smites the waters, and they are halved, here and there, and they pass over both of them on dry land.
2.9: And it comes to pass, at their passing over, that Elijah has said to Elisha, `Ask, what do I do for you before I am taken from you?' and Elisha says, `Then let there be, I pray you, a double portion of your spirit to me;'
2.10: and he says, `You have asked a hard thing; if you do see me taken from you, it is to you so; and if not, it is not.'
2.11: And it comes to pass, they are going, going on and speaking, and indeed, a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and they separate between them both, and Elijah goes up in a whirlwind, to the heavens.
2.12: And Elisha is seeing, and he is crying, `My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and its horsemen;' and he has not seen him again; and he takes hold on his garments, and rends them into two pieces.
2.13: And he takes up the robe of Elijah, that fell from off him, and turns back and stands on the edge of the Jordan,
2.14: and he takes the robe of Elijah that fell from off him, and smites the waters, and says, `Where is Jehovah, God of Elijah--even He?' and he smites the waters, and they are halved, here and there, and Elisha passes over.
2.15: And they see him--the sons of the prophets who are in Jericho--over-against, and they say, `Rested has the spirit of Elijah on Elisha;' and they come to meet him, and bow themselves to him to the earth,
2.16: and say to him, `Indeed, we pray you, there are with your servants fifty men, sons of valour: let them go, we pray you, and they seek your lord, lest the Spirit of Jehovah has taken him up, and does cast him on one of the hills, or into one of the valleys;' and he says, `You do not send.'
2.17: And they press upon him, till he is ashamed, and he says, `Send you;' and they send fifty men, and they seek three days, and have not found him;
2.18: and they turn back to him--and he is abiding in Jericho--and he says to them, `Did I not say to you, Do not go?'
2.19: And the men of the city say to Elisha, `Indeed, we pray you, the site of the city is good, as my lord sees, and the waters are bad, and the earth sterile.'
2.20: And he says, `Bring to me a new dish, and place there salt;' and they bring it to him,
2.21: and he goes out to the source of the waters, and casts there salt, and says, `Thus said Jehovah, I have given healing to these waters; there is not from there any more death and sterility.'
2.22: And the waters are healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha, that he spoke.
2.23: And he goes up from there to Beth-El, and he is going up in the way, and little youths have come out from the city, and scoff at him, and say to him, `Go up, bald-head! go up, bald-head!'
2.24: And he looks behind him, and sees them, and declares them vile in the name of Jehovah, and two bears come out of the forest, and rend of them forty and two lads.
2.25: And he goes from there to the hill of Carmel, and from there he has turned back to Samaria.

3.1: And Jehoram son of Ahab has reigned over Israel, in Samaria, in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigns twelve years,
3.2: and does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, only not like his father, and like his mother, and he turns aside the standing-pillar of Baal that his father made;
3.3: only to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat that he caused Israel to sin he has cleaved, he has not turned aside from it.
3.4: And Mesha king of Moab was a sheep-master, and he rendered to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs, and a hundred thousand rams, with wool,
3.5: and it comes to pass at the death of Ahab, that the king of Moab transgresses against the king of Israel.
3.6: And king Jehoram goes out in that day from Samaria, and inspects all Israel,
3.7: and goes and sends to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, `The king of Moab has transgressed against me; do you go with me to Moab for battle?' and he says, `I go up, as I, so you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses.
3.8: And he says, `Where is this--the way we go up?' and he says, `The way of the wilderness of Edom.'
3.9: And the king of Israel goes, and the king of Judah, and the king of Edom, and they turn round the way seven days, and there has been no water for the camp, and for the cattle that are at their feet,
3.10: and the king of Israel says, `Alas, for Jehovah has called for these three kings, to give them into the hand of Moab.'
3.11: And Jehoshaphat says, `Is there not here a prophet of Jehovah, and we seek Jehovah by him?' And one of the servants of the king of Israel answers and says, `Here is Elisha son of Shaphat, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.'
3.12: And Jehoshaphat says, `The word of Jehovah is with him;' and go down to him do the king of Israel, and Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom.
3.13: And Elisha says to the king of Israel, `What--to me and to you? go to the prophets of your father, and to the prophets of your mother;' and the king of Israel says to him, `No, for Jehovah has called for these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab.'
3.14: And Elisha says, `Jehovah of Hosts lives, before whom I have stood; for unless the face of Jehoshaphat king of Judah I am lifting up, I do not look to you, nor see you;
3.15: and now, bring to me a minstrel; and it has been, at the playing of the minstrel, that the hand of Jehovah is on him,
3.16: and he says, `Thus said Jehovah, Make this valley ditches--ditches;
3.17: for thus said Jehovah, You do not see wind, nor do you see rain, and that valley is full of water, and you have drunk--you, and your cattle, and your beasts.
3.18: `And this has been light in the eyes of Jehovah, and he has given Moab into your hand,
3.19: and you have smitten every fenced city, and every choice city, and every good tree you cause to fall, and all fountains of waters you stop, and every good portion you mar with stones.'
3.20: And it comes to pass in the morning, at the ascending of the morning -present, that indeed, waters are coming in from the way of Edom, and the land is filled with the waters,
3.21: and all Moab have heard that the kings have come up to fight against them, and they are called together, from every one girding on a girdle and upward, and they stand by the border.
3.22: And they rise early in the morning, and the sun has shone on the waters, and the Moabites see, from over-against, the waters red as blood,
3.23: and say, `Blood this is; the kings have been surely destroyed, and they smite each his neighbour; and now for spoil, Moab!'
3.24: And they come in to the camp of Israel, and the Israelites rise, and smite the Moabites, and they flee from their face; and they enter into Moab, so as to smite Moab,
3.25: and the cities they break down, and on every good portion they cast each his stone, and have filled it, and every fountain of water they stop, and every good tree they cause to fall--till one had left its stones in Kir-Haraseth, and the slingers go round and smite it.
3.26: And the king of Moab sees that the battle has been too strong for him, and he takes with him seven hundred men, drawing sword, to cleave through to the king of Edom, and they have not been able,
3.27: and he takes his son, the first-born who reigns in his stead, and causes him to ascend--a burnt-offering on the wall, and there is great wrath against Israel, and they journey from off him, and turn back to the land.

4.1: And a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets has cried to Elisha, saying, `Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you have known that your servant was fearing Jehovah, and the lender has come to take my two children to him for servants.'
4.2: And Elisha says to her, `What do I do for you? declare to me, what have you in the house?' and she says, `Your maid-servant has nothing in the house except a pot of oil.'
4.3: And he says, `Go, ask for you vessels from without, from all your neighbours--empty vessels--let them not be few;
4.4: and you have entered, and shut the door upon you, and upon your sons, and have poured out into all these vessels, and the full ones you do remove.'
4.5: And she goes from him, and shuts the door upon her, and upon her sons; they are bringing nigh to her, and she is pouring out,
4.6: and it comes to pass, at the filling of the vessels, that she says to her son, `Bring nigh to me a vessel more,' and he says to her, `There is not a vessel more;' and the oil stays.
4.7: And she comes and declares to the man of God, and he says, `Go, sell the oil, and repay your loan; and you and your sons do live of the rest.'
4.8: And the day comes that Elisha passes over to Shunem, and there is a great woman, and she lays hold on him to eat bread, and it comes to pass, at the time of his passing over, he turns aside there to eat bread,
4.9: and she says to her husband, `Indeed, I pray you, I have known that a holy man of God he is, passing over by us continually;
4.10: let us make, I pray you, a little upper chamber of the wall, and we set for him there a bed, and a table, and a high seat, and a candlestick; and it has been, in his coming in to us, he does turn aside there.'
4.11: And the day comes, that he comes in there, and turns aside to the upper chamber, and lies there,
4.12: and he says to Gehazi his young man, `Call for this Shunammite;' and he calls for her, and she stands before him.
4.13: And he says to him, `Say, I pray you, to her, Indeed, you have troubled yourself concerning us with all this trouble; what--to do for you? is it to speak for you to the king, or to the head of the host?' and she says, `In the midst of my people I am dwelling.'
4.14: And he says, `And what--to do for her?' and Gehazi says, `Truly she has no son, and her husband is aged.'
4.15: And he says, `Call for her;' and he calls for her, and she stands at the opening,
4.16: and he says, `At this season, according to the time of life, you are embracing a son;' and she says, `No, my lord, O man of God, do not lie to your maid-servant.'
4.17: And the woman conceives and bears a son, at this season, according to the time of life, that Elisha spoke of to her.
4.18: And the lad grows, and the day comes that he goes out to his father, to the reapers,
4.19: and he says to his father, `My head, my head;' and he says to the young man, `Bear him to his mother;'
4.20: and he bears him, and brings him in to his mother, and he sits on her knees till the noon, and dies.
4.21: And she goes up, and lays him on the bed of the man of God, and shuts the door upon him, and goes out,
4.22: and calls to her husband, and says, `Send, I pray you, to me, one of the young men, and one of the asses, and I run to the man of God, and return.'
4.23: And he says, `Wherefore are you going to him to-day? --neither new moon nor sabbath!' and she says, `Peace to you!'
4.24: And she saddles the ass, and says to her young man, `Lead, and go, do not restrain riding for me, except I have said so to you.'
4.25: And she goes, and comes in to the man of God, to the hill of Carmel, and it comes to pass, at the man of God's seeing her from over-against, that he says to Gehazi his young man, `Indeed, this Shunammite;
4.26: now, run, I pray you, to meet her, and say to her, Is there peace to you? is there peace to your husband? is there peace to the lad?' and she says, `Peace.'
4.27: And she comes in to the man of God, to the hill, and lays hold on his feet, and Gehazi comes nigh to thrust her away, and the man of God says, `Let her alone, for her soul is bitter to her, and Jehovah has hidden it from me, and has not declared it to me.'
4.28: And she says, `Did I ask a son from my lord? did I not say, Do not deceive me?'
4.29: And he says to Gehazi, `Gird up your loins, and take my staff in your hand, and go; when you do meet a man, you do not salute him; and when a man does salute you, you do not answer him; and you have laid my staff on the face of the youth.'
4.30: And the mother of the youth says, `Jehovah lives, and your soul lives--if I leave you;' and he rises and goes after her.
4.31: And Gehazi has passed on before them, and lays the staff on the face of the youth, and there is no voice, and there is no attention, and he turns back to meet him, and declares to him, saying, `The youth has not awaked.'
4.32: And Elisha comes in to the house, and indeed, the youth is dead, laid on his bed,
4.33: and he goes in and shuts the door upon them both, and prays to Jehovah.
4.34: And he goes up, and lies down on the lad, and puts his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands, and stretches himself upon him, and the flesh of the lad becomes warm;
4.35: and he turns back and walks in the house, once here and once there, and goes up and stretches himself upon him, and the youth sneezeth till seven times, and the youth opens his eyes.
4.36: And he calls to Gehazi, and says, `Call to this Shunammite;' and he calls her, and she comes in to him, and he says, `Lift up your son.'
4.37: And she goes in, and falls at his feet, and bows herself to the earth, and lifts up her son, and goes out.
4.38: And Elisha has turned back to Gilgal, and the famine is in the land, and the sons of the prophets are sitting before him, and he says to his young man, `Set on the great pot, and boil pottage for the sons of the prophets.'
4.39: And one goes out to the field to gather herbs, and finds a vine of the field, and gathers of it gourds of the field--the fulness of his garment--and comes in and splits them into the pot of pottage, for they knew them not;
4.40: and they pour out for the men to eat, and it comes to pass at their eating of the pottage, that they have cried out, and say, `Death is in the pot, O man of God!' and they have not been able to eat.
4.41: And he says, `Then bring you meal;' and he casts into the pot, and says, `Pour out for the people, and they eat;' and there was no evil thing in the pot.
4.42: And a man has come from Baal-Shalishah, and brings in to the man of God bread of first-fruits, twenty loaves of barley, and full ears of corn in its husk, and he says, `Give to the people, and they eat.'
4.43: And his minister says, `What--do I give this before a hundred men?' and he says, `Give to the people, and they eat, for thus said Jehovah, Eat and leave;'
4.44: and he gives before them, and they eat and leave, according to the word of Jehovah.

5.1: And Naaman, head of the host of the king of Aram, was a great man before his lord, and accepted of face, for by him had Jehovah given salvation to Aram, and the man was mighty in valour--leprous.
5.2: And the Aramaeans have gone out by troops, and they take captive out of the land of Israel a little damsel, and she is before the wife of Naaman,
5.3: and she says to her mistress, `O that my lord were before the prophet who is in Samaria; then he does recover him from his leprosy.'
5.4: And one goes in and declares to his lord, saying, `Thus and thus she has spoken, the damsel who is from the land of Israel.'
5.5: And the king of Aram says, `Go you, enter, and I send a letter to the king of Israel;' and he goes and takes in his hand ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of garments.
5.6: And he brings in the letter to the king of Israel, saying, `And now, at the coming in of this letter to you, indeed, I have sent to you Naaman my servant, and you have recovered him from his leprosy.'
5.7: And it comes to pass, at the king of Israel's reading the letter, that he rends his garments, and says, `Am I God, to put to death and to keep alive, that this one is sending to me to recover a man from his leprosy? for surely know, I pray you, and see, for he is presenting himself to me.'
5.8: And it comes to pass, at Elisha the man of God's hearing that the king of Israel has rent his garments, that he sends to the king, saying, `Why have you rent your garments? let him come, I pray you, to me, and he does know that there is a prophet in Israel.'
5.9: And Naaman comes, with his horses and with his chariot, and stands at the opening of the house for Elisha;
5.10: and Elisha sends to him a messenger, saying, `Go, and you have washed seven times in Jordan, and your flesh does turn back to you--and be you clean.
5.11: And Naaman is wroth, and goes on, and says, `Indeed, I said, To me he does certainly come out, and has stood and called in the name of Jehovah his God, and waved his hand over the place, and recovered the leper.
5.12: Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? do I not wash in them and I have been clean?' and he turns and goes on in fury.
5.13: And his servants come nigh, and speak to him, and say, `My father, a great thing had the prophet spoken to you--do you not do it? and surely, when he has said to you, Wash, and be clean.'
5.14: And he goes down and dips in Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh does turn back as the flesh of a little youth, and is clean.
5.15: And he turns back to the man of God, he and all his camp, and comes in, and stands before him, and says, `Indeed, I pray you, I have known that there is not a God in all the earth except in Israel; and now, take, I pray you, a blessing from your servant.'
5.16: And he says, `Jehovah lives, before whom I have stood--if I take it;' and he presses on him to take, and he refuses.
5.17: And Naaman says, `If not--let be given, I pray you, to your servant, a couple of mules' burden of earth, for your servant does make no more burnt-offering and sacrifice to other gods, but to Jehovah.
5.18: For this thing Jehovah be propitious to your servant, in the coming in of my lord into the house of Rimmon to bow himself there, and he was supported by my hand, and I bowed myself in the house of Rimmon; for my bowing myself in the house of Rimmon Jehovah be propitious, I pray you, to your servant in this thing.'
5.19: And he says to him, `Go in peace.' And he goes from him a kibrath of land,
5.20: And Gehazi, servant of Elisha the man of God, says, `Indeed, my lord has spared Naaman this Aramaean, not to receive from his hand that which he brought; Jehovah lives; surely if I have run after him, then I have taken from him something.'
5.21: And Gehazi pursues after Naaman, and Naaman sees one running after him, and alights from off the chariot to meet him, and says, `Is there peace?'
5.22: And he says, `Peace; my lord has sent me, saying, Indeed, now, this, come to me have two young men from the hill-country of Ephraim, of the sons of the prophets; give, I pray you, to them, a talent of silver, and two changes of garments.'
5.23: And Naaman says, `Be pleased, take two talents;' and he urges on him, and binds two talents of silver in two purses, and two changes of garments, and gives to two of his young men, and they bear before him;
5.24: and he comes in to the high place, and takes out of their hand, and lays up in the house, and sends away the men, and they go.
5.25: And he has come in, and does stand by his lord, and Elisha says to him, `From where--Gehazi?' and he says, `Your servant went not here or there.'
5.26: And he says to him, `My heart went not when the man turned from off his chariot to meet you; is it a time to take silver, and to take garments, and olives, and vines, and flock, and herd, and men-servants, and maid-servants?
5.27: yes, the leprosy of Naaman does cleave to you, and to your seed, --to the age;' and he goes out from before him--leprous as snow.

6.1: And sons of the prophet say to Elisha, `Indeed, we pray you, the place where we are dwelling before you is too strait for us;
6.2: let us go, we pray you, to the Jordan, and we take from there each one beam, and we make for ourselves there a place to dwell there;' and he says, `Go.'
6.3: And the one says, `Be pleased, I pray you, and go with your servants;' and he says, `I--I go.'
6.4: And he goes with them, and they come in to the Jordan, and cut down the trees,
6.5: and it comes to pass, the one is felling the beam, and the iron has fallen into the water, and he cries and says, `Alas! my lord, and it asked!'
6.6: And the man of God says, `Where has it fallen?' and he shows him the place, and he cuts a stick, and casts there, and causes the iron to swim,
6.7: and says, `Raise to you;' and he puts forth his hand and takes it.
6.8: And the king of Aram has been fighting against Israel, and takes counsel with his servants, saying, `At such and such a place is my encamping.'
6.9: And the man of God sends to the king of Israel, saying, `Take heed of passing by this place, for there are the Aramaeans coming down;
6.10: and the king of Israel sends to the place of which the man of God spoke to him, and warned him, and he is preserved there not once nor twice.
6.11: And the heart of the king of Aram is tossed about concerning this thing, and he calls to his servants, and says to them, `Do you not declare to me who of us is for the king of Israel?'
6.12: And one of his servants says, `No, my lord, O king, for Elisha the prophet, who is in Israel, declares to the king of Israel the words that you speak in the inner part of your bed-chamber.'
6.13: And he says, `Go you and see where he is, and I send and take him;' and it is declared to him, saying, `Indeed--in Dothan.'
6.14: And he sends there horses and chariot, and a heavy force, and they come in by night, and go round against the city.
6.15: And the servant of the man of God rises early, and goes out, and indeed, a force is surrounding the city, and horse and chariot, and his young man says to him, `Alas! my lord, how do we do?'
6.16: And he says, `Fear not, for more are they who are with us than they who are with them.'
6.17: And Elisha prays, and says, `Jehovah, open, I pray You, his eyes, and he does see;' and Jehovah opens the eyes of the young man, and he sees, and indeed, the hill is full of horses and chariots of fire, round about Elisha.
6.18: And they come down to it, and Elisha prays to Jehovah, and says, `Smite, I pray You, this nation with blindness;' and He smites them with blindness, according to the word of Elisha.
6.19: And Elisha says to them, `This is not the way, nor is this the city; come after me, and I lead you to the man whom you seek;' and he leads them to Samaria.
6.20: And it comes to pass, at their coming in to Samaria, that Elisha says, `Jehovah, open the eyes of these, and they see;' and Jehovah opens their eyes, and they see, and indeed, in the midst of Samaria!
6.21: And the king of Israel says to Elisha, at his seeing them, `Do I smite--do I smite--my father?'
6.22: And he says, `You do not smite; those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow are you smiting? set bread and water before them, and they eat, and drink, and go to their lord.'
6.23: And he prepares for them great provision, and they eat and drink, and he sends them away, and they go to their lord: and troops of Aram have not added any more to come in to the land of Israel.
6.24: And it comes to pass afterwards, that Ben-Hadad king of Aram gathers all his camp, and goes up, and lays siege to Samaria,
6.25: and there is a great famine in Samaria, and indeed, they are laying siege to it, till the head of an ass is at eighty silverlings, and a forth of the cab of dovesdung at five silverlings.
6.26: And it comes to pass, the king of Israel is passing by on the wall, and a woman has cried to him, saying, `Save, my lord, O king.'
6.27: And he says, `Jehovah does not save you--from where do I save you? out of the threshing-floor, or out of the wine-vat?'
6.28: And the king says to her, `What--to you?' and she says, `This woman said to me, Give your son, and we eat him to-day, and my son we eat to-morrow;
6.29: and we boil my son and eat him, and I say to her on the next day, Give your son, and we eat him; and she hides her son.'
6.30: And it comes to pass, at the king's hearing the words of the woman, that he rends his garments, and he is passing by on the wall, and the people see, and indeed, the sackcloth is on his flesh within.
6.31: And he says, `Thus does God do to me, and thus He does add--if it remain--the head of Elisha son of Shaphat--upon him this day.'
6.32: And Elisha is sitting in his house, and the elders are sitting with him, and the king sends a man from before him; before the messenger does come to him, even he himself said to the elders, `Have you seen that this son of the murderer has sent to turn aside my head? see, at the coming in of the messenger, shut the door, and you have held him fast at the door, is not the sound of the feet of his lord behind him?'
6.33: He is yet speaking with them, and indeed, the messenger is coming down to him, and he says, `Indeed, this is the evil from Jehovah: what--do I wait for Jehovah any more?'

7.1: And Elisha says, `Hear you a word of Jehovah: thus said Jehovah, About this time to-morrow, a measure of fine flour is at a shekel, and two measures of barley at a shekel, in the gate of Samaria.'
7.2: And the captain whom the king has, by whose hand he has been supported, answers the man of God and says, `Indeed, Jehovah is making windows in the heavens--shall this thing be?' and he says, `Indeed, you are seeing it with your eyes, and of it you do not eat.'
7.3: And four men have been leprous, at the opening of the gate, and they say one to another, `What--we are sitting here till we have died;
7.4: if we have said, We go in to the city, then the famine is in the city, and we have died there; and if we have sat here, then we have died; and now, come and we fall to the camp of Aram; if they keep us alive, we live, and if they put us to death--we have died.'
7.5: And they rise in the twilight, to go in to the camp of Aram, and they come in to the extremity of the camp of Aram, and indeed, there is not a man there,
7.6: seeing Jehovah has caused the camp of Aram to hear a noise of chariot and a noise of horse--a noise of great force, and they say one to another, `Indeed, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites, and the kings of Egypt, to come against us.'
7.7: And they rise and flee in the twilight, and forsake their tents, and their horses, and their asses--the camp as it is --and flee for their life.
7.8: And these lepers come in to the extremity of the camp, and come in to one tent, and eat, and drink, and lift up from there silver, and gold, and garments, and go and hide; and they turn back and go in to another tent, and lift up from there, and go and hide.
7.9: And they say one to another, `We are not doing right this day; a day of tidings it is, and we are keeping silent; and--we have waited till the light of the morning, then has punishment found us; and now, come and we go in and declare to the house of the king.'
7.10: And they come in, and call to the gatekeeper of the city, and declare for themselves, saying, `We have come in to the camp of Aram, and indeed, there is not there a man, or sound of man, but the bound horse, and the bound ass, and tents as they are.'
7.11: and he calls the gatekeepers, and they declare to the house of the king within.
7.12: And the king rises by night, and says to his servants, `Let me declare, I pray you, to you that which the Aramaeans have done to us; they have known that we are famished, and they are gone out from the camp to be hidden in the field, saying, When they come out from the city, then we catch them alive, and to the city we enter.'
7.13: And one of his servants answers and says, `Then let them take, I pray you, five of the horses that are left, that have been left in it--indeed, they are as all the multitude of Israel who have been left in it; indeed, they are as all the multitude of Israel who have been consumed--and we send and see.'
7.14: And they take two chariot-horses, and the king sends after the camp of Aram, saying, `Go, and see.'
7.15: And they go after them to the Jordan, and indeed, all the way is full of garments and vessels that the Aramaeans have cast away in their haste, and the messengers turn back and declare to the king.
7.16: And the people go out and spoil the camp of Aram, and there is a measure of fine flour at a shekel, and two measures of barley at a shekel, according to the word of Jehovah.
7.17: And the king has appointed the captain, by whose hand he is supported, over the gate, and the people tread him down in the gate, and he dies, as the man of God spoke, which he spoke in the coming down of the king to him,
7.18: yes, it comes to pass, according to the speaking of the man of God to the king, saying, `Two measures of barley at a shekel, and a measure of fine flour at a shekel are, at this time to-morrow, in the gate of Samaria;'
7.19: and the captain answers the man of God, and says, `And indeed, Jehovah is making windows in the heavens--it is according to this word?' and he says, `Indeed, you are seeing with your eyes, and of it you do not eat;'
7.20: and it comes to him so, and the people tread him down in the gate, and he dies.

8.1: And Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had revived, saying, `Rise and go, you and your household, and sojourn where you do sojourn, for Jehovah has called for a famine, and also, it is coming to the land seven years.'
8.2: And the woman rises, and does according to the word of the man of God, and goes, she and her household, and sojourns in the land of the Philistines seven years.
8.3: And it comes to pass, at the end of seven years, that the woman turns back from the land of the Philistines, and goes out to cry to the king, for her house, and for her field.
8.4: And the king is speaking to Gehazi, servant of the man of God, saying, `Recount, I pray you, to me, the whole of the great things that Elisha has done.'
8.5: And it comes to pass, he is recounting to the king how he had revived the dead, and indeed, the woman whose son he had revived is crying to the king, for her house and for her field, and Gehazi says, `My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this her son, whom Elisha revived.'
8.6: And the king asks at the woman, and she recounts to him, and the king appoints to her a certain eunuch, saying, `Give back all that she has, and all the increase of the field from the day of her leaving the land even till now.'
8.7: And Elisha comes in to Damascus, and Ben-Hadad king of Aram is sick, and it is declared to him, saying, `The man of God has come here.'
8.8: And the king says to Hazael, `Take in your hand a present, and go to meet the man of God, and you have sought Jehovah by him, saying, Do I revive from this sickness?'
8.9: And Hazael goes to meet him, and takes a present in his hand, even of every good thing of Damascus, a burden of forty camels, and he comes in and stands before him, and says, `Your son Ben-Hadad, king of Aram, has sent me to you, saying, Do I revive from this sickness?'
8.10: And Elisha says to him, `Go, say, You do certainly not revive, seeing Jehovah has showed me that he does surely die.'
8.11: And he sets his face, yes, he sets it till he is ashamed, and the man of God weeps.
8.12: And Hazael says, `Wherefore is my lord weeping?' and he says, `Because I have known the evil that you do to the sons of Israel--their fenced places you do send into fire, and their young men with sword you do slay, and their sucklings you do dash to pieces, and their pregnant women you do rip up.'
8.13: And Hazael says, `But what, is your servant the dog, that he does this great thing?' And Elisha says, `Jehovah has showed me you--king of Aram.'
8.14: And he goes from Elisha, and comes in to his lord, and he says to him, `What said Elisha to you?' and he says, `He said to me, You do certainly recover.'
8.15: And it comes to pass on the morrow, that he takes the coarse cloth, and dips in water, and spreads on his face, and he dies, and Hazael reigns in his stead.
8.16: And in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel--and Jehoshaphat is king of Judah--has Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah reigned;
8.17: a son of thirty and two years was he in his reigning, and eight years he has reigned in Jerusalem.
8.18: And he walks in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab, for a daughter of Ahab was to him for a wife, and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah,
8.19: and Jehovah was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David his servant, as He said to him, to give to him a lamp--to his sons all the days.
8.20: In his days has Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and they cause a king to reign over them,
8.21: and Joram passes over to Zair, and all the chariots with him, and he himself has risen by night, and smites Edom, that is coming round about to him, and the heads of the chariots, and the people flees to its tents;
8.22: and Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah till this day; then does Libnah revolt at that time.
8.23: And the rest of the matters of Joram, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
8.24: And Joram lies with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in the city of David, and reign does Ahaziah his son in his stead.
8.25: In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel reigned has Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah;
8.26: a son of twenty and two years is Ahaziah in his reigning, and one year he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Athaliah daughter of Omri king of Israel,
8.27: and he walks in the way of the house of Ahab, and does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, like the house of Ahab, for he is son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
8.28: And he goes with Joram son of Ahab to battle with Hazael king of Aram in Ramoth-Gilead, and the Aramaeans smite Joram,
8.29: and Joram the king turns back to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds with which the Arameans smite him in Ramah, in his fighting with Hazael king of Aram, and Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah has gone down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, for he is sick.

9.1: And Elisha the prophet has called to one of the sons of the prophets, and says to him, `Gird up your loins, and take this vial of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-Gilead,
9.2: and you have gone in there, and see you there Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, and you have gone in, and caused him to rise out of the midst of his brethren, and brought him in to the inner part of an inner-chamber,
9.3: and taken the vial of oil, and poured on his head, and said, Thus said Jehovah, I have anointed you for king to Israel; and you have opened the door, and fled, and do not wait.'
9.4: And the young man goes--the young man the prophet--to Ramoth-Gilead,
9.5: and comes in, and indeed, chiefs of the force are sitting, and he says, `I have a word to you, O chief!' and Jehu says, `To which of all of us?' and he says, `To you, O chief.'
9.6: And he rises and comes in to the house, and he pours the oil on his head, and says to him, `Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, I have anointed you for king to the people of Jehovah, to Israel,
9.7: and you have smitten the house of Ahab your lord, and I have required the blood of My servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of Jehovah, from the hand of Jezebel;
9.8: and perished has all the house of Ahab, and I have cut off to Ahab those sitting on the wall, and restrained, and left, in Israel,
9.9: and I have given up the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and as the house of Baasha son of Ahijah,
9.10: and Jezebel do the dogs eat in the portion of Jezreel, and there is none burying;' and he opens the door and flees.
9.11: And Jehu has gone out to the servants of his lord, and one says to him, `Is there peace? wherefore came this madman to you?' and he says to them, `You have known the man and his talk.'
9.12: And they say, `False, declare, we pray you, to us;' and he says, `Thus and thus spoke he to me, saying, Thus said Jehovah, I have anointed you for king to Israel.'
9.13: And they haste and take each his garment, and put it under him at the top of the stairs, and blow with a trumpet, and say, `Reigned has Jehu!'
9.14: And Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspires against Joram--(and Joram was keeping in Ramoth-Gilead, he and all Israel, from the presence of Hazael king of Aram,
9.15: and king Joram turns back to be healed in Jezreel, of the wounds with which the Aramaeans smite him, in his fighting with Hazael king of Aram) --and Jehu says, `If it is your mind, let not an escaped one go out from the city, to go to declare it in Jezreel.'
9.16: And Jehu rides, and goes to Jezreel, for Joram is lying there, and Ahaziah king of Judah has gone down to see Joram.
9.17: And the watchman is standing on the tower in Jezreel, and sees the company of Jehu in his coming, and says, `A company I see;' and Joram says, `Take a rider and send to meet them, and let him say, Is there peace?'
9.18: and the rider on the horse goes to meet him, and says, `Thus said the king, Is there peace?' and Jehu says, `What--to you and to peace? turn round behind me.' And the watchman declares, saying, `The messenger came to them, and he has not returned.'
9.19: And he sends a second rider on a horse, and he comes in to them, and says, `Thus said the king, Is there peace?' and Jehu says, `What--to you and to peace? turn round behind me.'
9.20: And the watchman declares, saying, `He came to them, and he has not returned, and the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for with madness he drives.'
9.21: And Jehoram says, `Harness;' and his chariot is harnessed, and Jehoram king of Israel goes out, and Ahaziah king of Judah, each in his chariot, and they go out to meet Jehu, and find him in the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite.
9.22: And it comes to pass, at Jehoram's seeing Jehu, that he says, `Is there peace, Jehu?' and he says, `What is the peace, while the whoredoms of Jezebel your mother, and her witchcrafts, are many?'
9.23: And Jehoram turns his hands, and flees, and says to Ahaziah, `Deceit, O Ahaziah!'
9.24: And Jehu has filled his hand with a bow, and smites Jehoram between his arms, and the arrow goes out from his heart, and he bows down in his chariot.
9.25: And Jehu says to Bidkar his captain, `Lift up, cast him into the portion of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite--for, remember, I and you were riding together after Ahab his father, and Jehovah lifted upon him this burden:
9.26: Have I not the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons seen yesternight--the affirmation of Jehovah--yes, I have recompensed to you in this portion--the affirmation of Jehovah; --and now, lift up, cast him into the portion, according to the word of Jehovah.'
9.27: And Ahaziah king of Judah has seen, and flees the way of the garden-house, and Jehu pursues after him, and says, `Smite him--also him--in the chariot,' in the going up to Gur, that is Ibleam, and he flees to Megiddo, and dies there,
9.28: and his servants carry him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and bury him in his burying-place, with his fathers, in the city of David.
9.29: And in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab reign did Ahaziah over Judah.
9.30: And Jehu comes in to Jezreel, and Jezebel has heard, and puts her eyes in paint and makes right her head, and looks out through the window.
9.31: And Jehu has come into the gate, and she says, `Was there peace to Zimri--slayer of his lord?'
9.32: And he lifts up his face to the window, and says, `Who is with me? --who?' and look out to him do two or three eunuchs;
9.33: And he says, `Let her go;' and they let her go, and some of her blood is sprinkled on the wall, and on the horses, and he treads her down.
9.34: And he comes in, and eats, and drinks, and says, `Look after, I pray you, this cursed one, and bury her, for she is a king's daughter.'
9.35: And they go to bury her, and have not found of her except the skull, and the feet, and the palms of the hands.
9.36: And they turn back, and declare to him, and he says, `The word of Jehovah it is, that He spoke by the hand of this servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the portion of Jezreel do the dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel,
9.37: and the carcase of Jezebel has been as dung on the face of the field in the portion of Jezreel, that they say not, This is Jezebel.'

10.1: And Ahab has seventy sons in Samaria, and Jehu writes letters, and sends to Samaria, to the heads of Jezreel, the elders, and to the supporters of Ahab, saying,
10.2: `And now, at the coming in of this letter to you, and with you are sons of your lord, and with you are the chariots and the horses, and a fenced city, and the armour,
10.3: and you have seen the best and the upright of the sons of your lord, and have set him on the throne of his father, and fight you for the house of your lord.'
10.4: And they fear very greatly, and say, `Indeed, the two kings have not stood before him, and how do we stand--we?'
10.5: And he who is over the house, and he who is over the city, and the elders, and the supporters, send to Jehu, saying, `Your servants we are, and all that you say to us we do; we do not make any one king--that which is good in your eyes do.'
10.6: And he writes to them a letter a second time, saying, `If you are for me, and to my voice are hearkening, take the heads of the men--the sons of your lord, and come to me about this time to-morrow, to Jezreel;' and the sons of the king are seventy men, with the great ones of the city those bringing them up.
10.7: And it comes to pass, at the coming in of the letter to them, that they take the sons of the king, and slaughter seventy men, and put their heads in baskets, and send to him to Jezreel,
10.8: and the messenger comes in, and declares to him, saying, `They have brought in the heads of the sons of the king,' and he says, `Make them two heaps at the opening of the gate till the morning.'
10.9: And it comes to pass in the morning, that he goes out, and stands, and says to all the people, `Righteous are you; indeed, I have conspired against my lord, and slay him--and who smote all these?
10.10: Know you now, that nothing does fall of the word of Jehovah to the earth that Jehovah spoke against the house of Ahab, and Jehovah has done that which He spoke by the hand of His servant Elijah.'
10.11: And Jehu smites all those left to the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, and his acquaintances, and his priests, till he has not left to him a remnant.
10.12: And he rises, and comes in and goes to Samaria; he is at the shepherds' shearing-house in the way,
10.13: and Jehu has found the brethren of Ahaziah king of Judah, and says, `Who are you?' and they say, `Brethren of Ahaziah we are, and we go down to salute the sons of the king, and the sons of the mistress.'
10.14: And he says, `Catch them alive;' and they catch them alive, and slaughter them at the pit of the shearing-house, forty and two men, and he has not left a man of them.
10.15: And he goes from there, and finds Jehonadab son of Rechab--to meet him, and blesses him, and says to him, `Is your heart right, as my heart is with your heart?' and Jehonadab says, `It is;' --`Then it is; give your hand;' and he gives his hand, and he causes him to come up into him into the chariot,
10.16: and says, `Come with me, and look on my zeal for Jehovah;' and they cause him to ride in his chariot.
10.17: And he comes in to Samaria, and smites all those left to Ahab in Samaria, till his destroying him, according to the word of Jehovah that He spoke to Elisha.
10.18: And Jehu gathers the whole of the people, and says to them, `Ahab served Baal a little--Jehu does serve him much:
10.19: and now, all the prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests, call you to me; let not a man be lacking, for a great sacrifice I have for Baal; every one who is lacking--he does not live;' and Jehu has done it in subtilty, in order to destroy the servants of Baal.
10.20: And Jehu says, `Sanctify a restraint for Baal;' and they proclaim it.
10.21: And Jehu sends into all Israel, and all the servants of Baal come in, and there has not been left a man who has not come in; and they come in to the house of Baal, and the house of Baal is full--mouth to mouth.
10.22: And he says to him who is over the wardrobe, `Bring out clothing to all servants of Baal;' and he brings out to them the clothing.
10.23: And Jehu goes in, and Jehonadab son of Rechab, to the house of Baal, and says to the servants of Baal, `Search and see, lest there be here with you of the servants of Jehovah--but, the servants of Baal by themselves.'
10.24: And they come in to make sacrifices and burnt-offerings, and Jehu has set for himself in an out-place eighty men, and says, `The man who lets escape any of the men whom I am bringing in to your hand--his soul for his soul.'
10.25: And it comes to pass at his finishing to make the burnt-offering, that Jehu says to the runners, and to the captains, `Go in, smite them, let none come out;' and they smite them by the mouth of the sword, and the runners and the captains cast them out; and they go to the city, to the house of Baal,
10.26: and bring out the standing-pillars of the house of Baal, and burn them,
10.27: and break down the standing-pillar of Baal, and break down the house of Baal, and appoint it for a draught-house to this day.
10.28: And Jehu destroys Baal out of Israel,
10.29: only--the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, that he caused Israel to sin, Jehu has not turned aside from after them--the calves of gold that are at Beth-El, and in Dan.
10.30: And Jehovah says to Jehu, `Because that you have done well, to do that which is right in My eyes--according to all that is in My heart you have done to the house of Ahab--the sons of the fourth generation do sit for you on the throne of Israel.'
10.31: And Jehu has not taken heed to walk in the law of Jehovah, God of Israel, with all his heart, he has not turned aside from the sins of Jeroboam, that he caused Israel to sin.
10.32: In those days has Jehovah begun to cut off some in Israel, and Hazael smites them in all the border of Israel,
10.33: from the Jordan, at the sun-rising, the whole land of Gilead, of the Gadite, and the Reubenite, and the Manassahite (from Aroer, that is by the brook Arnon), even Gilead and Bashan.
10.34: And the rest of the matters of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his might, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
10.35: And Jehu lies with his fathers, and they bury him in Samaria, and reign does Jehoahaz his son in his stead.
10.36: And the days that Jehu has reigned over Israel are twenty and eight years, in Samaria.

11.1: And Athaliah is mother of Ahaziah, and she has seen that her son is dead, and she rises, and destroys all the seed of the kingdom;
11.2: and Jehosheba daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, takes Joash son of Ahaziah, and steals him out of the midst of the sons of the king who are put to death, him and his nurse, in the inner part of the bed-chambers, and they hide him from the presence of Athaliah, and he has not been put to death,
11.3: and he is with her, in the house of Jehovah, hiding himself, six years, and Athaliah is reigning over the land.
11.4: And in the seventh year has Jehoiada sent and takes the heads of the hundreds, of the executioners and of the runners, and brings them in to him, to the house of Jehovah, and makes with them a covenant, and causes them to swear in the house of Jehovah, and shows them the son of the king,
11.5: and commands them, saying, `This is the thing that you do; The third of you are going in on the sabbath, and keepers of the charge of the house of the king,
11.6: and the third is at the gate of Sur, and the third at the gate behind the runners, and you have kept the charge of the house pulled down;
11.7: and two parts of you, all going out on the sabbath--they have kept the charge of the house of Jehovah about the king,
11.8: and you have compassed the king round about, each with his weapons in his hand, and he who is coming to the ranges is put to death; and be you with the king in his going out and in his coming in.'
11.9: And the heads of the hundreds do according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded, and take each his men going in on the sabbath, with those going out on the sabbath, and come in to Jehoiada the priest,
11.10: and the priest gives to the heads of the hundreds the spears and the shields that king David had, that are in the house of Jehovah.
11.11: And the runners stand, each with his weapons in his hand, from the right shoulder of the house to the left shoulder of the house, by the altar and by the house, by the king round about;
11.12: and he brings out the son of the king, and puts on him the crown, and the testimony, and they make him king, and anoint him, and smite the hand, and say, `Let the king live.'
11.13: And Athaliah hears the voice of the runners and of the people, and she comes in to the people, to the house of Jehovah,
11.14: and looks, and indeed, the king is standing by the pillar, according to the ordinance, and the heads, and the trumpets, are by the king, and all the people of the land are rejoicing, and blowing with trumpets, and Athaliah rends her garments, and calls, `Conspiracy! conspiracy!'
11.15: And Jehoiada the priest commands the heads of the hundreds, inspectors of the force, and says to them, `Bring her out to the outside of the ranges, and him who is going after her, put to death by the sword:' for the priest had said, `Let her not be put to death in the house of Jehovah.'
11.16: And they make for her sides, and she enters the way of the entering in of the horses to the house of the king, and is put to death there.
11.17: And Jehoiada makes the covenant between Jehovah and the king and the people, to be for a people to Jehovah, and between the king and the people.
11.18: And all the people of the land go in to the house of Baal, and break it down, its altars and its images they have thoroughly broken, and Mattan priest of Baal they have slain before the altars; and the priest sets inspectors over the house of Jehovah,
11.19: and takes the heads of the hundreds, and the executioners, and the runners, and all the people of the land, and they bring down the king from the house of Jehovah, and come by the way of the gate of the runners, to the house of the king, and he sits on the throne of the kings.
11.20: And all the people of the land rejoice, and the city is quiet, and Athaliah they have put to death by the sword in the house of the king;
11.21: a son of seven years is Jehoash in his reigning.

12.1: In the seventh year of Jehu reigned has Jehoash, and forty years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Zibiah of Beer-Sheba,
12.2: and Jehoash does that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah all his days in which Jehoiada the priest directed him,
12.3: only, the high places have not turned aside, still are the people sacrificing and making perfume in high places.
12.4: And Jehoash says to the priests, `All the money of the sanctified things that is brought in to the house of Jehovah, the money of him who is passing over, each the money of his valuation, all the money that it goes up on the heart of a man to bring in to the house of Jehovah,
12.5: do the priests take to them, each from his acquaintance, and they strengthen the breach of the house, in all places where there is found a breach.'
12.6: And it comes to pass, in the twenty and third year of king Jehoash, the priests have not strengthened the breach of the house,
12.7: and king Jehoash calls to Jehoiada the priest, and to the priests, and says to them, `Wherefore are you not strengthening the breach of the house? and now, receive no money from your acquaintances, but for the breach of the house give it.'
12.8: And the priests consent not to receive money from the people, nor to strengthen the breach of the house,
12.9: and Jehoiada the priest takes a chest, and pierces a hole in its lid, and puts it near the altar, on the right side, as one comes in to the house of Jehovah, and the priests keeping the threshold have put there all the money that is brought in to the house of Jehovah.
12.10: And it comes to pass, at their seeing that the money is abundant in the chest, that there goes up a scribe of the king, and of the high priest, and they bind it up, and count the money that is found in the house of Jehovah,
12.11: and have given the weighed money into the hands of those doing the work, those inspecting the house of Jehovah, and they bring it out to those working in the wood, and to builders who are working in the house of Jehovah,
12.12: and to those repairing the wall, and to hewers of stone, and to buy wood and hewn stones to strengthen the breach of the house of Jehovah, and for all that goes out on the house, to strengthen it.
12.13: Only, there is not made for the house of Jehovah basins of silver, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, any vessel of gold, and vessel of silver, out of the money that is brought into the house of Jehovah;
12.14: for to those doing the work they give it, and they have strengthened with it the house of Jehovah,
12.15: and they do not reckon with the men into whose hand they give the money to give to those doing the work, for in faithfulness they are dealing.
12.16: The money of a trespass-offering, and the money of sin-offerings is not brought in to the house of Jehovah--for the priests it is.
12.17: Then go up does Hazael king of Aram, and fights against Gath, and captures it, and Hazael sets his face to go up against Jerusalem;
12.18: and Jehoash king of Judah takes all the sanctified things that Jehoshaphat, and Jehoram, and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, had sanctified, and his own sanctified things, and all the gold that is found in the treasures of the house of Jehovah and of the house of the king, and sends to Hazael king of Aram, and he goes up from off Jerusalem.
12.19: And the rest of the matters of Joash, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
12.20: And his servants rise, and make a conspiracy, and smite Joash in the house of Millo, that is going down to Silla:
12.21: yes, Jozachar son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad son of Shemer, his servants, have smitten him, and he dies, and they bury him with his fathers in the city of David, and reign does Amaziah his son, in his stead.

13.1: In the twenty and third year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah, has Jehoahaz son of Jehu reigned over Israel, in Samaria--seventeen years,
13.2: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and goes after the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, that he caused Israel to sin--he turned not aside from it,
13.3: and the anger of Jehovah burns against Israel, and He gives them into the hand of Hazael king of Aram, and into the hand of Ben-Hadad son of Hazael, all the days.
13.4: And Jehoahaz appeases the face of Jehovah, and Jehovah hearkens to him, for He has seen the oppression of Israel, for oppressed them has the king of Aram, --
13.5: and Jehovah gives to Israel a saviour, and they go out from under the hand of Aram, and the sons of Israel dwell in their tents as heretofore;
13.6: only, they have not turned aside from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, that he caused Israel to sin, in it they walked, and also, the shrine has remained in Samaria, --
13.7: for he left not to Jehoahaz of the people except fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen, for the king of Aram has destroyed them, and makes them as dust for threshing.
13.8: And the rest of the matters of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
13.9: And Jehoahaz lies with his fathers, and they bury him in Samaria, and reign does Joash his son in his stead.
13.10: In the thirty and seventh year of Joash king of Judah reigned has Jehoash son of Jehoahaz over Israel, in Samaria--sixteen years,
13.11: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, he has not turned aside from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, that he caused Israel to sin, in it he walked.
13.12: And the rest of the matters of Joash, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
13.13: And Joash lies with his fathers, and Jeroboam has sat on his throne, and Joash is buried in Samaria, with the kings of Israel.
13.14: And Elisha has been sick with his sickness in which he dies, and come down to him does Joash king of Israel, and weeps on his face, and says, `My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and its horsemen.'
13.15: And Elisha says to him, `Take bow and arrows:' and he takes to him bow and arrows.
13.16: And he says to the king of Israel, `Place your hand on the bow;' and he places his hand, and Elisha puts his hands on the hands of the king,
13.17: and says, `Open the window eastward;' and he opens, and Elisha says, `Shoot,' and he shoots; and he says, `An arrow of salvation to Jehovah, and an arrow of salvation against Aram, and you have smitten Aram, in Aphek, till consuming.'
13.18: And he says, `Take the arrows,' and he takes; and he says to the king of Israel, `Smite to the earth;' and he smites three times, and stays.
13.19: And the man of God is wroth against him, and says, `By smiting five or six times then you had smitten Aram till consuming; and now, three times you do smite Aram.'
13.20: And Elisha dies, and they bury him, and troops of Moab come in to the land, at the coming in of the year,
13.21: and it comes to pass, they are burying a man, and indeed, they have seen the troop, and cast the man into the grave of Elisha, and the man goes and comes against the bones of Elisha, and lives, and rises on his feet.
13.22: And Hazael king of Aram has oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz,
13.23: and Jehovah does favour them, and pity them, and turn to them, for the sake of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and has not been willing to destroy them, nor to cast them from His presence as yet.
13.24: And Hazael king of Aram dies, and reign does Ben-Hadad his son in his stead,
13.25: and Jehoash son of Jehoahaz turns and takes the cities out of the hand of Ben-Hadad son of Hazael that he had taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father in war; three times has Joash smitten him, and he brings back the cities of Israel.

14.1: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel reigned has Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah;
14.2: a son of twenty and five years was he in his reigning, and twenty and nine years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Jehoaddan of Jerusalem,
14.3: and he does that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah, only not like David his father, according to all that Joash his father did he has done,
14.4: only, the high places have not turned aside--yet are the people sacrificing and making perfume in high places.
14.5: And it comes to pass, when the kingdom has been strong in his hand, that he smites his servants, those smiting the king his father,
14.6: and the sons of those smiting him he has not put to death, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses that Jehovah commanded, saying, `Fathers are not put to death for sons, and sons are not put to death for fathers, but each for his own sin is put to death.'
14.7: He has smitten Edom, in the valley of salt--ten thousand, and seized Selah in war, and one calls its name Joktheel to this day,
14.8: then has Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, `Come, we look one another in the face.'
14.9: And Jehoash king of Israel sends to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, `The thorn that is in Lebanon has sent to the cedar that is in Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son for a wife; and pass by does a beast of the field that is in Lebanon, and treads down the thorn.
14.10: You have certainly smitten Edom, and your heart has lifted you up; be honoured, and abide in your house; and why do you stir yourself up in evil, that you have fallen, you, and Judah with you?'
14.11: And Amaziah has not hearkened, and go up does Jehoash king of Israel, and they look one another in the face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, in Beth-Shemesh, that is Judah's,
14.12: and Judah is smitten before Israel, and they flee each to his tent.
14.13: And Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, caught has Jehoash king of Israel in Beth-Shemesh, and they come in to Jerusalem, and he bursts through the wall of Jerusalem, at the gate of Ephraim to the gate of the corner, four hundred cubits,
14.14: and has taken all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that are found in the house of Jehovah, and in the treasures of the house of the king, and the sons of the pledges, and turns back to Samaria.
14.15: And the rest of the matters of Jehoash that he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
14.16: And Jehoash lies with his fathers, and is buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and reign does Jeroboam his son in his stead.
14.17: And Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lives after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years,
14.18: and the rest of the matters of Amaziah are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
14.19: And they make a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he flees to Lachish, and they send after him to Lachish, and put him to death there,
14.20: and lift him up on the horses, and he is buried in Jerusalem, with his fathers, in the city of David.
14.21: And all the people of Judah take Azariah, and he is a son of sixteen years, and cause him to reign instead of his father Amaziah;
14.22: he has built Elath, and brings it back to Judah, after the lying of the king with his fathers.
14.23: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, reigned has Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel in Samaria--forty and one years,
14.24: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, he has not turned aside from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat that he caused Israel to sin.
14.25: He has brought back the border of Israel, from the entering in of Hamath to the sea of the desert, according to the word of Jehovah, God of Israel, that He spoke by the hand of His servant Jonah son of Amittai the prophet, who is of Gath-Hepher,
14.26: for Jehovah has seen the affliction of Israel--very bitter, and there is none restrained, and there is none left, and there is no helper to Israel;
14.27: and Jehovah has not spoken to blot out the name of Israel from under the heavens, and saves them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.
14.28: And the rest of the matters of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought, and with which he brought back Damascus, and Hamath of Judah, into Israel, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
14.29: And Jeroboam lies with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and reign does Zechariah his son in his stead.

15.1: In the twenty and seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel reigned has Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah,
15.2: a son of sixteen years was he in his reigning, and fifty and two years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Jecholiah of Jerusalem,
15.3: and he does that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah, according to all that Amaziah his father did,
15.4: only, the high places have not turned aside--yet are the people sacrificing and making perfume in high places.
15.5: And Jehovah smites the king, and he is a leper to the day of his death, and he dwells in a separate house, and Jotham son of the king is over the house, judging the people of the land.
15.6: And the rest of the matters of Azariah, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
15.7: And Azariah lies with his fathers, and they bury him with his fathers, in the city of David, and reign does Jotham his son in his stead.
15.8: In the thirty and eighth year of Azariah king of Judah reigned has Zechariah son of Jeroboam over Israel, in Samaria, six months,
15.9: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, as did his fathers, he has not turned aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat that he caused Israel to sin.
15.10: And Shallum son of Jabesh conspires against him, and smites him before the people, and puts him to death, and reigns in his stead.
15.11: And the rest of the matters of Zechariah, indeed, they are written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.
15.12: It is the word of Jehovah that He spoke to Jehu, saying, `Sons of the fourth generation do sit for you on the throne of Israel;' and it is so.
15.13: Shallum son of Jabesh has reigned in the thirty and ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigns a month of days in Samaria;
15.14: and go up does Menahem son of Gadi from Tirzah and comes in to Samaria, and smites Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria, and puts him to death, and reigns in his stead.
15.15: And the rest of the matters of Shallum, and his conspiracy that he made, indeed, they are written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.
15.16: Then does Menahem smite Tiphsah, and all who are in it, and its borders from Tirzah, for it opened not to him, and he smites it, all its pregnant women he has ripped up.
15.17: In the thirty and ninth year of Azariah king of Judah reigned has Menahem son of Gadi over Israel--ten years in Samaria.
15.18: And he does the evil in the eyes of Jehovah, he has turned not aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat that he caused Israel to sin, all his days.
15.19: Pul king of Asshur has come against the land, and Menahem gives to Pul a thousand talents of silver, for his hand being with him to strengthen the kingdom in his hand.
15.20: And Menahem brings out the silver from Israel, from all the mighty men of wealth, to give to the king of Asshur, fifty shekels of silver for each one, and the king of Asshur turns back and has not stayed there in the land.
15.21: And the rest of the matters of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
15.22: And Menahem lies with his fathers, and reign does Pekahiah his son in his stead.
15.23: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah has Pekahiah son of Menahem reigned over Israel, in Samaria--two years,
15.24: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, he has not turned aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat that he caused Israel to sin.
15.25: And Pekah son of Remaliah, his captain, does conspire against him, and smites him in Samaria, in the high place of the house of the king with Argob and Arieh, and with him fifty men of the sons of the Gileadites, and he puts him to death, and reigns in his stead.
15.26: And the rest of the matters of Pekahiah, and all that he did, indeed, they are written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.
15.27: In the fifty and second year of Azariah king of Judah, reigned has Pekah son of Remaliah over Israel, in Samaria--twenty years,
15.28: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, he has not turned aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, that he caused Israel to sin.
15.29: In the days of Pekah king of Israel has Tiglath-Pileser king of Asshur come, and takes Ijon, and Abel-Beth-Maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and removes them to Asshur.
15.30: And make a conspiracy does Hoshea son of Elah against Pekah son of Remaliah, and smites him, and puts him to death, and reigns in his stead, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
15.31: And the rest of the matters of Pekah, and all that he did, indeed, they are written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.
15.32: In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel reigned has Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah.
15.33: A son of twenty and five years was he in his reigning, and sixteen years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Jerusha daughter of Zadok,
15.34: and he does that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah, according to all that Uzziah his father did he has done.
15.35: Only, the high places have not turned aside--yet are the people sacrificing and making perfume in high places; he has built the high gate of the house of Jehovah.
15.36: And the rest of the matters of Jotham, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
15.37: In those days has Jehovah begun to send against Judah Rezin king of Amram and Pekah son of Remaliah.
15.38: And Jotham lies with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers, in the city of David his father, and reign does Ahaz his son in his stead.

16.1: In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah reigned has Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah.
16.2: A son of twenty years is Ahaz in his reigning, and sixteen years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and he has not done that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah his God, like David his father,
16.3: and he walks in the way of the kings of Israel, and also his son he has caused to pass over into fire, according to the abominations of the nations that Jehovah dispossessed from the presence of the sons of Israel,
16.4: and he sacrifices and makes perfume in high places, and on the heights, and under every green tree.
16.5: Then does Rezin king of Aram go up, and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel, to Jerusalem, to battle, and they lay siege to Ahaz, and they have not been able to fight.
16.6: At that time has Rezin king of Aram brought back Elath to Aram, and casts out the Jews from Elath, and the Aramaeans have come in to Elath, and dwell there to this day.
16.7: And Ahaz sends messengers to Tiglath-Pileser king of Asshur, saying, `Your servant and your son am I; come up and save me out of the hand of the king of Aram, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me.'
16.8: And Ahaz takes the silver and the gold that is found in the house of Jehovah, and in the treasures of the house of the king, and sends to the king of Asshur--a bribe.
16.9: And hearken to him does the king of Asshur, and the king of Asshur goes up to Damascus, and seizes it, and removes the people of it to Kir, and Rezin he has put to death.
16.10: And king Ahaz goes to meet Tiglath-Pileser king of Asshur at Damascus, and sees the altar that is in Damascus, and king Ahaz sends to Urijah the priest the likeness of the altar, and its pattern, according to all its work,
16.11: and Urijah the priest builds the altar according to all that king Ahaz has sent from Damascus; so did Urijah the priest till the coming in of king Ahaz from Damascus.
16.12: And the king comes in from Damascus, and the king sees the altar, and the king draws near on the altar, and offers on it,
16.13: and perfumes his burnt-offering, and his present, and pours out his libation, and sprinkles the blood of the peace-offerings that he has, on the altar.
16.14: As to the altar of brass that is before Jehovah--he brings it near from the front of the house, from between the altar and the house of Jehovah, and puts it on the side of the altar, northward.
16.15: And king Ahaz commands him--Urijah the priest--saying, `On the great altar perfume the burnt-offering of the morning, and the present of the evening, and the burnt-offering of the king, and his present, and the burnt-offering of all the people of the land, and their present, and their libations; and all the blood of the burnt-offering, and all the blood of the sacrifice, on it you do sprinkle, and the altar of brass is to me to inquire by.'
16.16: And Urijah the priest does according to all that king Ahaz commanded.
16.17: And king Ahaz cuts off the borders of the bases, and turns aside from off them the laver, and the sea he has taken down from off the brazen oxen that are under it, and puts it on a pavement of stones.
16.18: And the covered place for the sabbath that they built in the house, and the entrance of the king without, he turned from the house of Jehovah, because of the king of Asshur.
16.19: And the rest of the matters of Ahaz that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
16.20: And Ahaz lies with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers, in the city of David, and reign does Hezekiah his son in his stead.

17.1: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah reigned has Hoshea son of Elah in Samaria, over Israel--nine years,
17.2: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, only, not as the kings of Israel who were before him;
17.3: against him came up Shalmaneser king of Asshur, and Hoshea is to him a servant, and does render to him a present.
17.4: And the king of Asshur finds in Hoshea a conspiracy, in that he has sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and has not caused a present to go up to the king of Asshur, as year by year, and the king of Asshur restrains him, and binds him in a house of restraint.
17.5: And the king of Asshur goes up into all the land, and he goes up to Samaria, and lays siege against it three years;
17.6: in the ninth year of Hoshea has the king of Asshur captured Samaria, and removes Israel to Asshur, and causes them to dwell in Halah, and in Habor, by the river Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
17.7: And it comes to pass, because the sons of Israel have sinned against Jehovah their God--who brings them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt--and fear other gods,
17.8: and walk in the statutes of the nations that Jehovah dispossessed from the presence of the sons of Israel, and of the kings of Israel that they made;
17.9: and the sons of Israel do covertly things that are not right against Jehovah their God, and build for them high places in all their cities, from a tower of the watchers to the fenced city,
17.10: and set up for them standing-pillars and shrines on every high height, and under every green tree,
17.11: and make perfume there in all high places, like the nations that Jehovah removed from their presence, and do evil things to provoke Jehovah,
17.12: and serve the idols, of which Jehovah said to them, `You do not do this thing;'
17.13: And Jehovah testifies against Israel, and against Judah, by the hand of every prophet, and every seer, saying, `Turn back from your evil ways, and keep My commands, My statutes, according to all the law that I commanded your fathers, and that I sent to you by the hand of My servants the prophets;'
17.14: and they have not hearkened, and harden their neck, like the neck of their fathers, who did not remain stedfast in Jehovah their God,
