17.15: and reject His statutes and His covenant that He made with their fathers, and His testimonies that He testified against them, and go after the vain thing, and become vain, and after the nations that are round about them, of whom Jehovah commanded them not to do like them;
17.16: And they forsake all the commands of Jehovah their God, and make to them a molten image--two calves, and make a shrine, and bow themselves to all the host of the heavens, and serve Baal,
17.17: and cause their sons and their daughters to pass over through fire, and divine divinations, and use enchantments, and sell themselves to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, to provoke Him;
17.18: That Jehovah shows himself very angry against Israel, and turns them aside from His presence; none has been left, only the tribe of Judah by itself.
17.19: Also Judah has not kept the commands of Jehovah their God, and they walk in the statutes of Israel that they had made.
17.20: And Jehovah kicks against all the seed of Israel, and afflicts them, and gives them into the hand of spoilers, till that He has cast them out of His presence,
17.21: for He has rent Israel from the house of David, and they make Jeroboam son of Nebat king, and Jeroboam drives Israel from after Jehovah, and has caused them to sin a great sin,
17.22: and the sons of Israel walk in all the sins of Jeroboam that he did, they have not turned aside from it,
17.23: till that Jehovah has turned Israel aside from His presence, as He spoke by the hand of all His servants the prophets, and Israel is removed from off its land to Asshur, to this day.
17.24: And the king of Asshur brings in from Babylon and from Cutha, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and causes them to dwell in the cities of Samaria instead of the sons of Israel, and they possess Samaria, and dwell in its cities;
17.25: and it comes to pass, at the commencement of their dwelling there, they have not feared Jehovah, and Jehovah does send among them the lions, and they are destroying among them.
17.26: And they speak to the king of Asshur, saying, `The nations that you have removed, and do place in the cities of Samaria, have not known the custom of the God of the land, and He sends among them the lions, and indeed, they are destroying them, as they do not know the custom of the God of the land.'
17.27: And the king of Asshur commands, saying, `Cause to go there one of the priests whom you removed from there, and they go and dwell there, and he does teach them the custom of the God of the land.'
17.28: And one of the priests whom they removed from Samaria comes in, and dwells in Beth-El, and he is teaching them how they do fear Jehovah,
17.29: and they are making each nation its gods, and place them in the houses of the high places that the Samaritans have made, each nation in their cities where they are dwelling.
17.30: And the men of Babylon have made Succoth-Benoth, and the men of Cuth have made Nergal, and the men of Hamath have made Ashima,
17.31: and the Avites have made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites are burning their sons with fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, gods of Sepharvim.
17.32: And they are fearing Jehovah, and make to themselves from their extremities priests of high places, and they are acting for them in the house of the high places.
17.33: Jehovah they are fearing, and their gods they are serving, according to the custom of the nations from where they removed them.
17.34: To this day they are doing according to the former customs--they are not fearing Jehovah, and are not doing according to their statutes, and according to their ordinances, and according to the law, and according to the command, that Jehovah commanded the sons of Jacob whose name He made Israel,
17.35: and Jehovah makes with them a covenant, and charges them, saying, `You do not fear other gods, nor bow yourselves to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them,
17.36: but Jehovah who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a stretched-out arm, Him you do fear, and to Him you bow yourselves, and to Him you do sacrifice;
17.37: and the statutes, and the judgments, and the law, and the command, that He wrote for you, you observe to do all the days, and you do not fear other gods;
17.38: and the covenant that I have made with you you do not forget, and you do not fear other gods;
17.39: but Jehovah your God you do fear, and He does deliver you out of the hand of all your enemies;'
17.40: and they have not hearkened, but according to their former custom they are doing,
17.41: and these nations are fearing Jehovah, and their graven images they have served, both their sons and their sons' sons; as their fathers did, they are doing to this day.

18.1: And it comes to pass, in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, reigned has Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah;
18.2: a son of twenty and five years was he in his reigning, and twenty and nine years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Abi daughter of Zechariah.
18.3: And he does that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah, according to all that David his father did,
18.4: he has turned aside the high places, and broken in pieces the standing-pillars, and cut down the shrine, and beaten down the brazen serpent that Moses made, for to these days were the sons of Israel making perfume to it, and he calls it `a piece of brass.'
18.5: In Jehovah, God of Israel, he has trusted, and after him there has not been like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among any who were before him;
18.6: and he cleaves to Jehovah, he has not turned aside from after Him, and keeps His commands that Jehovah commanded Moses.
18.7: And Jehovah has been with him, in every place where he goes out he acts wisely, and he rebels against the king of Asshur, and has not served him;
18.8: he has smitten the Philistines to Gaza, and its borders, from a tower of watchers to the fenced city.
18.9: And it comes to pass, in the fourth year of king Hezekiah--it is the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel--come up has Shalmaneser king of Asshur against Samaria, and lays siege to it,
18.10: and they capture it at the end of three years; in the sixth year of Hezekiah--it is the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel--has Samaria been captures,
18.11: and the king of Asshur removes Israel to Asshur, and placed them in Halah, and in Habor by the river Gozan, and in cities of the Medes,
18.12: because that they have not hearkened to the voice of Jehovah their God, and transgress His covenant--all that He commanded Moses, servant of Jehovah--yes, they have not hearkened nor done it.
18.13: And in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah has Sennacherib king of Asshur come up against all the fenced cities of Judah, and seizes them,
18.14: and Hezekiah king of Judah sends to the king of Asshur to Lachish, saying, `I have sinned, turn back from off me; that which you put on me I bear;' and the king of Asshur lays on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver, and thirty talents of gold,
18.15: and Hezekiah gives all the silver that is found in the house of Jehovah, and in the treasures of the house of the king;
18.16: at that time has Hezekiah cut off the doors of the temple of Jehovah, and the pillars that Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gives them to the king of Asshur.
18.17: And the king of Asshur sends Tartan, and the chief of the eunuchs, and the chief of the butlers, from Lachish, to king Hezekiah, with a heavy force, to Jerusalem, and they go up and come in to Jerusalem, and they go up, and come in and stand by the conduit of the upper pool that is in the highway of the fuller's field.
18.18: And they call to the king, and go out to them does Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who is over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the remembrancer.
18.19: And the chief of the butlers says to them, `Say, I pray you, to Hezekiah, Thus said the great king, the king of Asshur, What is this confidence in which you have confided?
18.20: You have said: Only a word of the lips! counsel and might are for battle; now, on whom have you trusted that you have rebelled against me?
18.21: `Now, indeed, you have trusted for you on the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt; which a man leans on, and it has gone into his hand, and pierced it! --so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all those trusting on him.
18.22: `And when you say to me, To Jehovah our God we have trusted, is it not He whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has turned aside, and says to Judah and to Jerusalem, Before this altar do you bow yourselves in Jerusalem?
18.23: `And, now, give a pledge for you, I pray you, to my lord the king of Asshur, and I give to you two thousand horses, if you are able to give for you riders on them.
18.24: And how do you turn back the face of one captain of the least of the servants of my lord, that you do trust for you on Egypt for chariot, and for horsemen?
18.25: Now, without Jehovah have I come up against this place to destroy it? Jehovah said to me, Go up against this land, and you have destroyed it.'
18.26: And Eliakim son of Hilkiah says--and Shebna, and Joah--to the chief of the butlers, `Speak, we pray you, to your servants in Aramaean, for we are understanding, and do not speak with us in Jewish, in the ears of the people who are on the wall.'
18.27: And the chief of the butlers says to them, `For your lord, and to you, has my lord sent me to speak these words? is it not for the men, those sitting on the wall to eat their own dung and to drink their own water, with you?'
18.28: And the chief of the butlers stands and calls with a great voice in Jewish, and speaks and says, `Hear you a word of the great king, the king of Asshur:
18.29: thus said the king, Let not Hezekiah lift you up, for he is not able to deliver you out of his hand;
18.30: and let not Hezekiah make you trust to Jehovah, saying, Jehovah does certainly deliver us, and this city is not given into the hand of the king of Asshur.
18.31: `Do not hearken to Hezekiah, for thus said the king of Asshur, Make with me a blessing, and come out to me, and eat you each of his vine, and each of his fig-tree, and drink you each the waters of his own well,
18.32: till my coming in, and I have taken you to a land like your own land, a land of corn and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of oil olive, and honey, and live, and die not; and do not hearken to Hezekiah, when he persuades you, saying, Jehovah does deliver us.
18.33: `Have the gods of the nations delivered at all each his land out of the hand of the king of Asshur?
18.34: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? where the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah, that they have delivered Samaria out of my hand?
18.35: Who are they among all the gods of the lands that have delivered their land out of my hand, that Jehovah does deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?'
18.36: And the people have kept silent, and have not answered him a word, for the command of the king is, saying, `Do not answer him.'
18.37: And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who is over the house, comes in, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the remembrancer, to Hezekiah, with rent garments, and they declare to him the words of the chief of the butlers.

19.1: And it comes to pass, at king Hezekiah's hearing, that he rends his garments, and covers himself with sackcloth, and enters the house of Jehovah,
19.2: and sends Eliakim, who is over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covering themselves with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, son of Amoz,
19.3: and they say to him, `Thus said Hezekiah--A day of distress, and rebuke, and despising is this day; for come have sons to the birth, and power there is not to bring forth.
19.4: `It may be Jehovah your God does hear all the words of the chief of the butlers with which the king of Asshur his lord has sent him to reproach the living God, and has decided concerning the words that Jehovah your God has heard, and you have lifted up prayer for the remnant that is found.'
19.5: And the servants of king Hezekiah come in to Isaiah,
19.6: and Isaiah says to them, `Thus do you say to your lord: Thus said Jehovah, Be not afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Asshur have reviled Me.
19.7: Indeed, I am giving in him a spirit, and he has heard a report, and has turned back to his land, and I have caused him to fall by the sword in his land.'
19.8: And the chief of the butlers turns back and finds the king of Asshur fighting against Libnah, for he has heard that he has journeyed from Lachish.
19.9: And he hears concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, saying, `Indeed, he has come out to fight with you;' and he turns and sends messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
19.10: `Thus do you speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, Let not your God lift you up in whom you are trusting, saying, Jerusalem is not given into the hand of the king of Asshur.
19.11: Indeed, you have heard that which the kings of Asshur have done to all the lands--to devote them; and you are delivered!
19.12: did the gods of the nations deliver them whom my fathers destroyed--Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the sons of Eden, who are in Thelassar?
19.13: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?'
19.14: And Hezekiah takes the letters out of the hand of the messengers, and reads them, and goes up to the house of Jehovah, and Hezekiah spreads it before Jehovah.
19.15: And Hezekiah prays before Jehovah, and says, `O Jehovah, God of Israel, inhabiting the cherubs, You are God Himself--Yourself alone--to all the kingdoms of the earth: You have made the heavens and the earth.
19.16: Incline, O Jehovah, Your ear, and hear; open, O Jehovah, Your eyes, and see; and hear You the words of Sennacherib with which he has sent him to reproach the living God.
19.17: `Truly, O Jehovah, kings of Asshur have laid waste the nations, and their land,
19.18: and have put their gods into fire, for they are no gods, but work of the hands of man, wood and stone, and destroy them.
19.19: And now, O Jehovah our God, save us, we pray You, out of his hand, and know do all kingdoms of the earth that You are Jehovah God--Yourself alone.'
19.20: And Isaiah son of Amoz sends to Hezekiah, saying, `Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, That which you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Asshur I have heard:
19.21: this is the word that Jehovah spoke concerning him: `Trampled on you--laughed at you, Has the virgin daughter of Zion Behind you shaken the head--Has the daughter of Jerusalem?
19.22: Whom have you reproached and reviled? And against whom lifted up a voice? Yes, you do lift up on high your eyes--Against the Holy One of Israel!
19.23: By the hand of your messengers You have reproached the Lord, and say: In the multitude of my chariots I have come up to a high place of mountains--The sides of Lebanon, And I cut down the height of its cedars, The choice of its firs, And I enter the lodging of its extremity, The forest of its Carmel.
19.24: I have digged, and drunk strange waters, And I dry up with the sole of my steps All floods of a bulwark.
19.25: Have you not heard from afar, it I made, From days of old that I formed it? Now I have brought it in, And it becomes a desolation, Ruinous heaps are fenced cities,
19.26: And their inhabitants are feeble-handed, They were broken down, and are dried up, They have been the herb of the field, And the greenness of the tender grass, Grass of the roofs, And blasted corn--before it has risen up!
19.27: And your sitting down, and your going out, And your coming in, I have known, And your anger toward Me;
19.28: Because of your anger toward Me, And your noise--it came up into My ears, I have put My hook in your nose, And My bridle in your lips, And have caused you to turn back, In the way in which you came.
19.29: And this to you is the sign, Food of the year is the spontaneous growth, And in the second year the self-produced, And in the third year sow you, and reap, And plant vineyards, and eat their fruits.
19.30: And it has continued--The escaped of the house of Judah That has been left--to take root beneath, And has made fruit upward.
19.31: For from Jerusalem goes out a remnant, And an escape from mount Zion; The zeal of Jehovah of Hosts does this.
19.32: Therefore, thus said Jehovah, Concerning the king of Asshur: He does not come in to this city, Nor does he shoot there an arrow, Nor does he come before it with shield. Nor does he pour out against it a mount.
19.33: In the way that he comes in--In it he turns back, And to this city he does not come in, The affirmation of Jehovah--
19.34: And I have covered over this city, To save it, for My own sake, And for the sake of David My servant.'
19.35: And it comes to pass, in that night, that a messenger of Jehovah goes out, and smites in the camp of Asshur a hundred eighty and five thousand, and they rise early in the morning, and indeed, all of them are dead corpses.
19.36: And Sennacherib king of Asshur journeys, and goes, and turns back, and dwells in Nineveh;
19.37: and it comes to pass, he is bowing himself in the house of Nisroch his god, and Adramelech and Sharezar his sons have smitten him with the sword, and they have escaped to the land of Ararat, and Esar-Haddon his son reigns in his stead.

20.1: In those days has Hezekiah been sick to death, and come to him does Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet, and says to him, `Thus said Jehovah: Give a charge to your house, for you are dying, and do not live.'
20.2: And he turns round his face to the wall, and prays to Jehovah, saying,
20.3: `I pray You, O Jehovah, remember, I pray You, how I have walked habitually before You in truth, and with a perfect heart, and that which is good in Your eyes I have done;' and Hezekiah weeps--a great weeping.
20.4: And it comes to pass--Isaiah has not gone out to the middle court--that the word of Jehovah has been to him, saying,
20.5: `Turn back, and you have said to Hezekiah, leader of My people: Thus said Jehovah, God of David your father, I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tear, indeed, I give healing to you, on the third day you do go up to the house of Jehovah;
20.6: and I have added to your days fifteen years, and out of the hand of the king of Asshur I deliver you and this city, and have covered over this city for My own sake, and for the sake of David My servant.'
20.7: And Isaiah says, `Take you a cake of figs;' and they take and lay it on the boil, and he revives.
20.8: And Hezekiah says to Isaiah, `What is the sign that Jehovah does give healing to me, that I have gone up on the third day to the house of Jehovah?'
20.9: And Isaiah says, `This is to you the sign from Jehovah, that Jehovah does the thing that He has spoken--The shadow has gone on ten degrees, or it does turn back ten degrees?'
20.10: And Hezekiah says, `It has been light for the shadow to incline ten degrees: no, but let the shadow turn backward ten degrees.'
20.11: And Isaiah the prophet calls to Jehovah, and He brings back the shadow by the degrees that it had gone down in the degrees of Ahaz--backward ten degrees.
20.12: At that time has Berodach-Baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a present to Hezekiah, for he heard that Hezekiah had been sick;
20.13: and Hezekiah hearkens to them, and shows them all the house of his treasury, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the good ointment, and all the house of his vessels, and all that has been found in his treasuries; there has not been a thing that Hezekiah has not showed them, in his house, and in all his dominion.
20.14: And Isaiah the prophet comes in to king Hezekiah, and says to him, `What said these men? and from where come they to you?' And Hezekiah says, `From a land afar off they have come--from Babylon.'
20.15: And he says, `What saw they in your house?' and Hezekiah says, `All that is in my house they saw; there has not been a thing that I have not showed them among my treasures.'
20.16: And Isaiah says to Hezekiah, `Hear a word of Jehovah:
20.17: Indeed, days are coming, and borne has been all that is in your house, and that your father have treasured up till this day, to Babylon; there is not left a thing, said Jehovah;
20.18: and of your sons who go out from you, whom you beget, they take away, and they have been eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.'
20.19: And Hezekiah says to Isaiah, `Good is the word of Jehovah that you have spoken;' and he says, `Is it not--if peace and truth are in my days?'
20.20: And the rest of the matters of Hezekiah, and all his might, and how he made the pool, and the conduit, and brings in the waters to the city, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
20.21: And Hezekiah lies with his fathers, and reign does Manasseh his son in his stead.

21.1: A son of twelve years is Manasseh in his reigning, and fifty and five years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Hephzi-Bah;
21.2: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, according to the abominations of the nations that Jehovah dispossessed from the presence of the sons of Israel,
21.3: and he turns and builds the high places that Hezekiah his father destroyed, and raises altars for Baal, and makes a shrine, as did Ahab king of Israel, and bows himself to all the host of the heavens, and serves them.
21.4: And he has built altars in the house of Jehovah, of which Jehovah said, `In Jerusalem I put My name.'
21.5: And he builds altars to all the host of the heavens in the two courts of the house of Jehovah;
21.6: and he has caused his son to pass through fire, and observed clouds, and used enchantment, and dealt with a familiar spirit and wizards; he has multiplied to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah--to provoke to anger.
21.7: And he sets the graven image of the shrine that he made in the house of which Jehovah said to David and to Solomon his son, `In this house, and in Jerusalem, that I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I put My name--to the age;
21.8: and I do not add to cause the foot of Israel to move from the ground that I gave to their fathers, only, if they observe to do according to all that I commanded them, and to all the law that My servant Moses commanded them.'
21.9: And they have not hearkened, and Manasseh causes them to err, to do the evil thing above the nations that Jehovah destroyed from the presence of the sons of Israel.
21.10: And Jehovah speaks by the hand of his servants the prophets, saying,
21.11: `Because that Manasseh king of Judah has done these abominations--he has done evil above all that the Amorites have done who are before him, and causes also Judah to sin by his idols;
21.12: therefore thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, Indeed, I am bringing in evil on Jerusalem and Judah, that whoever hears of it, tingle do his two ears.
21.13: And I have stretched out over Jerusalem the line of Samaria, and the plummet of the house of Ahab, and wiped Jerusalem as one wipes the dish--he has wiped, and has turned it on its face.
21.14: `And I have left the remnant of My inheritance, and given them into the hand of their enemies, and they have been for a prey and for a spoil to all their enemies,
21.15: because that they have done the evil thing in My eyes, and are provoking Me to anger from the day that their fathers came out of Egypt, even to this day.'
21.16: And also, innocent blood has Manasseh shed very much, till that he has filled Jerusalem--mouth to mouth; apart from his sin that he has caused Judah to sin, to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah.
21.17: And the rest of the matters of Manasseh, and all that he did, and his sin that he sinned, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
21.18: And Manasseh lies with his fathers, and is buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza, and reign does Amon his son in his stead.
21.19: A son of twenty and two years is Amon in his reigning, and two years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz of Jotbah,
21.20: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, as did Manasseh his father,
21.21: and walks in all the way that his father walked in, and serves the idols that his father served, and bows himself to them,
21.22: and forsakes Jehovah, God of his fathers, and has not walked in the way of Jehovah.
21.23: And the servants of Amon conspire against him, and put the king to death in his own house,
21.24: and the people of the land smite all those conspiring against king Amon, and the people of the land cause Josiah his son to reign in his stead.
21.25: And the rest of the matters of Amon that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
21.26: and one buries him in his burying-place in the garden of Uzza, and reign does Josiah his son in his stead.

22.1: A son of eight years is Josiah in his reigning, and thirty and one years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Jedidah daughter of Adaiah of Boskath,
22.2: and he does that which is right in the eyes of Jehovah, and walks in all the way of David his father, and has not turned aside--right or left.
22.3: And it comes to pass, in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, the king has sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the scribe, to the house of Jehovah, saying,
22.4: `Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, and he does complete the silver that is brought into the house of Jehovah, that the keepers of the threshold have gathered from the people,
22.5: and they give it into the hand of the doers of the work, the overseers, in the house of Jehovah, and they give it to the doers of the work that is in the house of Jehovah, to strengthen the breach of the house,
22.6: to artificers, and to builders, and to repairers of the wall, and to buy wood and hewn stones to strengthen the house;
22.7: only, the silver that is given into their hand is not reckoned with them, for in faithfulness they are dealing.
22.8: And Hilkiah the high priest says to Shaphan the scribe, `A book of the law I have found in the house of Jehovah;' and Hilkiah gives the book to Shaphan, and he reads it.
22.9: And Shaphan the scribe comes in to the king, and brings the king back word, and says, `Your servants have poured out the silver that has been found in the house, and give it into the hand of the doers of the work, the inspectors, in the house of Jehovah.'
22.10: And Shaphan the scribe declares to the king, saying, `A book has Hilkiah the priest given to me;' and Shaphan reads it before the king.
22.11: And it comes to pass, at the king's hearing the words of the book of the law, that he rends his garments,
22.12: and the king commands Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Achbor son of Michaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asahiah servant of the king, saying,
22.13: `Go, seek Jehovah for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is found, for great is the fury of Jehovah that is kindled against us, because that our fathers have not hearkened to the words of this book, to do according to all that is written for us.'
22.14: And Hilkiah the priest goes, and Ahikam, and Achbor, and Shaphan, and Asahiah, to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum, son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the garments, and she is dwelling in Jerusalem in the second, and they speak to her.
22.15: And she says to them, `Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, Say to the man who has sent you to me:
22.16: Thus said Jehovah, Indeed, I am bringing in evil to this place and on its inhabitants, all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read,
22.17: because that they have forsaken Me, and make perfume to other gods, so as to provoke Me to anger with every work of their hands, and My wrath has been kindled against this place, and it is not quenched.
22.18: `And to the king of Judah, who is sending you to seek Jehovah, thus do you say to him, Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, The words that you have heard--
22.19: because your heart is tender, and you are humbled because of Jehovah, in your hearing that which I have spoken against this place, and against its inhabitants, to be for a desolation, and for a reviling, and do rend your garments, and weep before Me--I also have heard--the affirmation of Jehovah--
22.20: therefore, indeed, I am gathering you to your fathers, and you have been gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes do not look on any of the evil that I am bringing in on this place;' and they bring the king back word.

23.1: And the king sends, and they gather to him all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem,
23.2: and the king goes up to the house of Jehovah, and every man of Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, with him, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the people, from small to great, and he reads in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that is found in the house of Jehovah.
23.3: And the king stands by the pillar, and makes the covenant before Jehovah, to walk after Jehovah, and to keep His commands, and His testimonies, and His statutes, with all the heart, and with all the soul, to establish the words of this covenant that are written on this book, and all the people stand in the covenant.
23.4: And the king commands Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the threshold, to bring out from the temple of Jehovah all the vessels that are made for Baal, and for the shrine, and for all the host of the heavens, and he burns them at the outside of Jerusalem, in the fields of Kidron, and has borne their ashes to Beth-El.
23.5: And he has caused to cease the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah have appointed, (and they make perfume in high places, in cities of Judah and suburbs of Jerusalem,) and those making perfume to Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the host of the heavens.
23.6: And he brings out the shrine from the house of Jehovah to the outside of Jerusalem, to the brook Kidron, and burns it at the brook Kidron, and beats it small to dust, and casts its dust on the grave of the sons of the people.
23.7: And he breaks down the houses of the whoremongers that are in the house of Jehovah, where the women are weaving houses for the shrine.
23.8: And he brings in all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiles the high places where the priests have made perfume, from Geba to Beer-Sheba, and has broken down the high places of the gates that are at the opening of the gate of Joshua, head of the city, that is on a man's left hand at the gate of the city;
23.9: only, the priests of the high places come not up to the altar of Jehovah in Jerusalem, but they have eaten unleavened things in the midst of their brethren.
23.10: And he has defiled Topheth, that is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, so that no man does cause his son and his daughter to pass over through fire to Molech.
23.11: And he causes to cease the horses that the kings of Judah have given to the sun from the entering in of the house of Jehovah, by the chamber of Nathan-Melech the eunuch, that is in the suburbs, and the chariots of the sun he has burnt with fire.
23.12: And the altars that are on the top of the upper chamber of Ahaz, that the kings of Judah made, and the altars that Manasseh made in the two courts of the house of Jehovah, has the king broken down, and removes from there, and has cast their dust to the brook Kidron.
23.13: And the high places that are on the front of Jerusalem, that are on the right of the mount of corruption, that Solomon king of Israel had built to Ashtoreth abomination of the Zidonians, and Chemosh abomination of Moab, and to Milcom abomination of the sons of Ammon, has the king defiled.
23.14: And he has broken in pieces the standing-pillars, and cuts down the shrines, and fills their place with bones of men;
23.15: and also the altar that is in Beth-El, the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat made, by which he made Israel sin, both that altar and the high place he has broken down, and does burn the high place--he has beat it small to dust, and has burnt the shrine.
23.16: And Josiah turns, and sees the graves that are there in the mount, and sends and takes the bones out of the graves, and burns them on the altar, and defiles it, according to the word of Jehovah that the man of God proclaimed, who proclaimed these things.
23.17: And he says, `What is this sign that I see?' and the men of the city say to him, `The grave of the man of God who has come from Judah, and proclaims these things that you have done concerning the altar of Beth-El.'
23.18: And he says, `Let him alone, let no man touch his bones;' and they let his bones escape, with the bones of the prophet who came out of Samaria.
23.19: And also all the houses of the high places that are in the cities of Samaria, that the kings of Israel made to provoke to anger, has Josiah turned aside, and does to them according to all the deeds that he did in Beth-El.
23.20: And he slays all the priests of the high places who are there by the altars, and burns the bones of man upon them, and turns back to Jerusalem.
23.21: And the king commands the whole of the people, saying, `Make you a passover to Jehovah your God, as it is written on this book of the covenant.'
23.22: Surely there has not been made like this passover from the days of the judges who judged Israel, even all the days of the kings of Israel, and of the kings of Judah;
23.23: but in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, has this passover been made to Jehovah in Jerusalem.
23.24: And also, those having familiar spirits, and the wizards, and the teraphim, and the idols, and all the abominations that were seen in the land of Judah, and in Jerusalem, has Josiah put away, in order to establish the words of the law that are written on the book that Hilkiah the priest has found in the house of Jehovah.
23.25: And like him there has not been before him a king who turned back to Jehovah with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses, and after him there has none risen like him.
23.26: Only, Jehovah has not turned back from the fierceness of His great anger with which His anger burned against Judah, because of all the provocations with which Manasseh provoked him,
23.27: and Jehovah says, `Also Judah I turn aside from my presence, as I turned Israel aside, and I have rejected this city that I have chosen--Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, My name is there.'
23.28: And the rest of the matters of Josiah, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
23.29: In his days has Pharaoh-Nechoh king of Egypt come up against the king of Asshur, by the river Phrat, and king Josiah goes out to meet him, and he puts him to death in Megiddo, when he sees him.
23.30: And his servants cause him to ride dying from Megiddo, and bring him in to Jerusalem, and bury him in his own grave, and the people of the land take Jehoahaz son of Josiah, and anoint him, and cause him to reign instead of his father.
23.31: A son of twenty and three years is Jehoahaz in his reigning, and three months he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah,
23.32: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, according to all that his fathers did,
23.33: and Pharaoh-Nechoh binds him in Riblah, in the land of Hamath, from reigning in Jerusalem, and he puts a fine on the land--a hundred talents of silver, and a talent of gold.
23.34: And Pharaoh-Nechoh causes Eliakim son of Josiah to reign instead of Josiah his father, and turns his name to Jehoiakim, and Jehoahaz he has taken away, and he comes in to Egypt, and dies there.
23.35: And the silver and the gold has Jehoiakim given to Pharaoh; only he valued the land to give the silver by the command of Pharaoh; from each, according to his valuation, he exacted the silver and the gold, from the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh-Nechoh.
23.36: A son of twenty and five years is Jehoiakim in his reigning, and eleven years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Zebudah daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah,
23.37: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, according to all that his fathers did.

24.1: In his days has Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come up, and Jehoiakim is to him a servant three years; and he turns and rebels against him,
24.2: and Jehovah sends against him the troops of the Chaldeans, and the troops of Aram, and the troops of Moab, and the troops of the sons of Ammon, and He sends them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of Jehovah, that He spoke by the hand of His servants the prophets;
24.3: only, by the command of Jehovah it has been against Judah to turn them aside from His presence, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did,
24.4: and also the innocent blood that he has shed, and he fills Jerusalem with innocent blood, and Jehovah was not willing to forgive.
24.5: And the rest of the matters of Jehoiakim, and all that he did, are they not written on the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
24.6: And Jehoiakim lies with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigns in his stead.
24.7: And the king of Egypt has not added any more to go out from his own land, for the king of Babylon has taken, from the brook of Egypt to the river Phrat, all that had been to the king of Egypt.
24.8: A son of eighteen years is Jehoiachin in his reigning, and three months he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem,
24.9: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, according to all that his fathers did.
24.10: At that time come up have servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Jerusalem, and the city goes into siege,
24.11: and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes against the city, and his servants are laying siege to it,
24.12: and Jehoiachin king of Judah goes out to the king of Babylon, he, and his mother, and his servants, and his chiefs, and his eunuchs, and the king of Babylon takes him in the eighth year of his reign,
24.13: and brings out from there all the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and the treasures of the house of the king, and cuts in pieces all the vessels of gold that Solomon king of Israel made in the temple of Jehovah, as Jehovah had spoken.
24.14: And he has removed all Jerusalem, and all the chiefs, and all the mighty ones of valour--ten thousand is the removal--and every artificer and smith, none has been left save the poor of the people of the land.
24.15: And he removes Jehoiachin to Babylon, and the mother of the king, and the wives of the king, and his eunuchs, and the mighty ones of the land--he has caused a removal to go from Jerusalem to Babylon,
24.16: and all the men of valour seven thousand, and the artificers and the smiths a thousand, the whole are mighty men, warriors; and the king of Babylon brings them in a captivity to Babylon.
24.17: And the king of Babylon causes Mattaniah his father's brother to reign in his stead, and turns his name to Zedekiah.
24.18: A son of twenty and one years is Zedekiah in his reigning, and eleven years he has reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother is Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah,
24.19: and he does the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah according to all that Jehoiakim did,
24.20: for, by the anger of Jehovah it has been against Jerusalem and against Judah, till he cast them out from His presence, that Zedekiah rebels against the king of Babylon.

25.1: And it comes to pass, in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth of the month, come has Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, he and all his force, against Jerusalem, and encamps against it, and builds against it a fortification round about.
25.2: And the city enters into siege till the eleventh year of king Zedekiah,
25.3: on the ninth of the month--when the famine is severe in the city, and there has not been bread for the people of the land,
25.4: then the city is broken up, and all the men of war go by night the way of the gate, between the two walls that are by the garden of the king, and the Chaldeans are against the city round about, and the king goes the way of the plain.
25.5: And the force of the Chaldeans pursue after the king, and overtake him in the plains of Jericho, and all his force have been scattered from him;
25.6: and they seize the king, and bring him up to the king of Babylon, to Riblah, and they speak with him--judgment.
25.7: And the sons of Zedekiah they have slaughtered before his eyes, and the eyes of Zedekiah he has blinded, and binds him with brazen fetters, and they bring him to Babylon.
25.8: And in the fifth month, on the seventh of the month (it is the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon), has Nebuzaradan chief of the executioners, servant of the king of Babylon, come to Jerusalem,
25.9: and he burns the house of Jehovah, and the house of the king, and all the houses of Jerusalem, yes, every great house he has burned with fire;
25.10: and the walls of Jerusalem round about have all the forces of the Chaldeans, who are with the chief of the executioners, broken down.
25.11: And the rest of the people, those left in the city, and those falling who have fallen to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude, has Nebuzaradan chief of the executioners removed;
25.12: and of the poor of the land has the chief of the executioners left for vine-dressers and for husbandmen.
25.13: And the pillars of brass that are in the house of Jehovah, and the bases, and the sea of brass, that is in the house of Jehovah, have the Chaldeans broken in pieces, and bear away their brass to Babylon.
25.14: And the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass with which they minister they have taken,
25.15: and the fire-pans, and the bowls that are wholly of silver, has the chief of the executioners taken.
25.16: The two pillars, the one sea, and the bases that Solomon made for the house of Jehovah, there was no weighing of the brass of all these vessels;
25.17: eighteen cubits is the height of the one pillar, and the chapiter on it is of brass, and the height of the chapiter is three cubits, and the net and the pomegranates are on the chapiter round about--the whole is of brass; and like these has the second pillar, with the net.
25.18: And the chief of the executioners takes Seraiah the head priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold,
25.19: and out of the city he has taken a certain eunuch who is appointed over the men of war, and five men of those seeing the king's face who have been found in the city, and the head scribe of the host, who musters the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who are found in the city,
25.20: and Nebuzaradan chief of the executioners takes them, and causes them to go to the king of Babylon, to Libnah,
25.21: and the king of Babylon smites them, and puts them to death in Riblah, in the land of Hamath, and he removes Judah from off its land.
25.22: And the people that is left in the land of Judah whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has left--he appoints over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.
25.23: And all the heads of the forces hear--they and the men--that the king of Babylon has appointed Gedaliah, and they come in to Gedaliah, to Mizpah, even Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Johanan son of Kareah, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maachathite--they and their men;
25.24: and Gedaliah swears to them, and to their men, and says to them, `Be not afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans, dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it is good for you.'
25.25: And it comes to pass, in the seventh month, come has Ishmael son of Nathaniah, son of Elishama of the seed of the kingdom, and ten men with him, and they smite Gedaliah, and he dies, and the Jews and the Chaldeans who have been with him in Mizpah.
25.26: And all the people rise, from small even to great, and the heads of the forces, and come in to Egypt, for they have been afraid of the presence of the Chaldeans.
25.27: And it comes to pass, in the thirty and seventh year of the removal of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the twenty and seventh of the month has Evil-Merodach king of Babylon lifted up, in the year of his reigning, the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, out of the house of restraint,
25.28: and speaks with him good things and puts his throne above the throne of the kings who are with him in Babylon,
25.29: and has changed the garments of his restraint, and he has eaten bread continually before him all days of his life,
25.30: and his allowance--a continual allowance--has been given to him from the king, the matter of a day in its day, all days of his life.
